excerpt: You have cut your debt from half your economy to four tenths in four years, and you hold iron, gold, gas and one of the richest seas of the Atlantic.
paras: You have cut your debt from half your economy to four tenths in four years, and you hold iron, gold, gas and one of the richest seas of the Atlantic. Nearly six in ten of your city dwellers live in slums. Let the sea and the gas build homes, water and schools.

Your partners are investing in your people. In June 2026 the International Monetary Fund approved a new programme over forty-two months, and the World Bank launched $40 million for IQRAA, quality education for all. In March 2026 it approved $240 million, shared with Benin, to protect your coasts and create jobs in the blue economy. The Islamic Development Bank has signed $59.28 million to bring electricity to isolated villages.

The work ahead is plain, and it is worth saying plainly. At the last count, in 2004, ninety-five in every hundred of your children reached the end of primary school unable to read a simple text, a figure so old that it must be measured again. Sixty-five in every hundred of you cannot always count on enough good food. Your health services reach 40 on the World Health Organization index. Reading sets your Coverage today, at 5.2 out of 100, with food and health close behind. Each of them is within your reach.

Now imagine that same resolve turned toward every home in the country. Picture Perfect Mauritania: a morning when every family cooks with clean fuel and sits down to a full table; when every tap runs clean and every home has a safe toilet; when every child walks to a school where a teacher is waiting, and reads with ease by the age of ten; when every mother lives within reach of a clinic with the lights on, and every young person finds work that pays. And no Mauritanian falls below a decent life, because the nation has decided that none will.
quote: The sea and the gas can build a home for every family. Let them.
